clue.text: Engineers heading up good clothing plant

indicators.note: placed at the top of a down-style build, so the engineers come first

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
finery is smart, showy dress

explanation.surface: Army engineers in charge of a factory that makes smart clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is an industrial plant where raw materials such as oil or sugar are purified.

clue.text: Review actor's debut in theatre with great approval

indicators.note: the actor's opening letter goes inside the theatre word

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter of actor's

parts.note: praise is warm approval

explanation.surface: A critic's review says an actor's first stage appearance met with acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappraise is to assess again, the same as reviewing something.

clue.text: Company that's cut down tree

indicators.note: cutting down a word shortens it, dropping its last letter here

parts.note: a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A timber company fells a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The fir is a kind of evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Disagreeable economies unravelling without the City

indicators.note: a thing unravelling comes apart, so the letters of economies are rearranged once the City's letters are set aside

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: Unpleasant cutbacks are coming apart once the financial district is left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you EC is removed: ECONOMIES minus E and C leaves NOMIOSE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or unpleasant, especially of a smell.

clue.text: In rugby, allowed champion no way to predominate

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
to let is to allow
a hero is a champion
O, zero, stands for no
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: In rugby, a star player is allowed no route to dominate the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To rule the roost is an idiom for being in charge and dominating others.

clue.text: Writer holding power in university environment

indicators.note: holding means wrapping round, so the writer's name goes around the power letter

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French novelist
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A novelist wields influence on a university site.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Check following snake that's seen on road

indicators.note: the check word comes after the snake word

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake
to check is to halt or stop

explanation.surface: Stopping after spotting a snake lying on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is the black tarry surfacing material laid on roads.

clue.text: Real patriot struggling for the working class

indicators.note: struggling suggests flailing about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A genuine nationalist fighting on behalf of the workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The proletariat is the Marxist term for wage-earning workers as a class.

clue.text: What's capital for Scotsman's chest

parts.note: with a capital letter the same word names a Channel Island

explanation.surface: Asking what a Scotsman keeps his capital in, as if in a strongbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' suggests a money box for 'capital', but capital means a capital letter: written Sark it is an island, and lowercase sark is a Scottish shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a Scots word for a shirt, and capitalised it is one of the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Lady with trio playing skilfully

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman performs with a group of three musicians, and plays deftly.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitly means cleverly and with dexterity.

clue.text: Clamour for invading Arab federation once

indicators.note: one word invading another is pushed inside it

parts.note: the UAR, United Arab Republic, joined Egypt and Syria from 1958 to 1961
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: An outcry in favour of invading a former Arab union.
explanation.definitionFit: Uproar is loud and confused clamour or protest.

clue.text: No small feeling after policeman receives millions in cash for injury

indicators.note: the feeling word comes after the policeman part
the policeman word receives, taking in, the millions letter

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman

indicators.note: no small means with the S for small taken away

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A hurt officer gets millions in a payout and no longer feels small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No small' strips the S from SENSATION to leave ENSATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensation is money awarded to someone for loss or injury.

clue.text: Support altering note ratio in scale

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: altering means changing, so these letters change their order

explanation.surface: A support structure modifies the note proportions on a musical scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Proportionate means in correct relative scale or ratio.

clue.text: Actor's missing out on one turn, a young leading role

indicators.note: missing out on something means leaving it out, so the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: Laurence Olivier, the British actor
I is the Roman numeral for one
a twist is a turn

explanation.surface: An actor is losing out on a single plot turn to a youthful lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the boy title character of Dickens's novel, a leading part for a young actor.

clue.text: Where one recalls written message nearly destroyed

parts.note: a memo is a written note or message

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A written note was almost wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip down memory lane is the idiom for reminiscing about the past.

clue.text: One helping to contain son's confidential remark

indicators.note: the helper word contains the son letter

parts.note: an aide is an assistant, one who helps
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An assistant struggles to restrain the boy who has whispered a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made privately, or on stage, meant not to be overheard.

clue.text: Living abroad loses right to write in great detail

indicators.note: the word loses a letter, so the right letter comes out

parts.note: an expatriate is someone living outside their native country

explanation.surface: Someone living overseas loses the right to be a long-winded writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject.

clue.text: Company involved in western processed food

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so CO goes inside the other letters
processed means worked on and transformed, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm takes part in making processed food in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western' reads as a film genre, but it is the letters to be reworked; 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize kernels eaten as a vegetable, a food.

clue.text: Opportunity to feed that is around mid-afternoon, primarily

indicators.note: the opportunity word goes around the feeding word

parts.note: time can mean an opportunity, as in a chance to do something
to eat is to feed

explanation.surface: A chance to eat at roughly the middle of the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' links the parts; the definition says the meal comes mainly in the middle of the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime is the late-afternoon break for tea, chiefly placed around the middle of the afternoon.

clue.text: Old liquid measures, not litres, seen around part of Ireland

indicators.note: seen around means turned round, so the letters read backwards
not litres means one L for litres is removed

parts.note: gills are small units of liquid volume, a quarter of a pint

explanation.surface: Antique quantities of drink, not metric ones, spotted somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one L from OGILLS gives OGILS, and 'seen around' turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Reported policeman lacking in spirit

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an inspector is a police rank; lacking the letters of in it becomes SPECTOR

explanation.surface: A police officer is said to be short of spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' tells you the spirit word only sounds like the shortened police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or phantom, a disembodied spirit.

clue.text: Ephemerally current changes to golf score, clearly

indicators.note: one letter changes to a new piece, which takes its place

parts.note: transiently means briefly, in a short-lived way
I is the physics symbol for electric current
par is the standard score for a golf hole

explanation.surface: A brief electrical current shifts to a golf score, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' swaps the I in TRANSIENTLY for PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparently means obviously, in a way that is easy to see through.

clue.text: Declared support for unelected politician

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge

explanation.surface: An announcement backing a lord who never stood for election.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer sits in the House of Lords, the UK upper house, without being elected.

clue.text: Bring out some plastic I left to go back

indicators.note: going back means the run is read from right to left
some means part of these words, so the run lies within them

explanation.surface: Get some plastic out, as I left it, to be returned.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'plastic I left' read backwards (TFELICITSALP) lies the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or evoke a response or information.

clue.text: Her Majesty's got in a state

definitions.meaning: the British queen who reigned from 1837 to 1901
an Australian state in the south-east, capital Melbourne

explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria was a monarch, and Victoria is also a state of Australia.

clue.text: Half-hearted support's to weaken

indicators.note: losing half the heart, one of the two middle letters drops out

parts.note: to root for someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A lukewarm backer is set to lose strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' is the verb, as in rooting for a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, so to waste away and weaken.

clue.text: More gunners paraded before the Queen

indicators.note: the gunners parade in front, coming first

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: Artillerymen march past the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather can mean more truly or more precisely, as in more accurately put.

clue.text: Upset with seat given by United Nations

indicators.note: the seat comes after, given alongside the nations' letters

parts.note: a settle is a wooden bench seat with a high back

explanation.surface: Disturbed at being given a chair by the United Nations.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is an old-fashioned bench seat, not 'settle' the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to upset or disturb someone.
